noteBlocks.md: Every carbon atom forms **four covalent bonds** — no more, no fewer. That one rule builds every structure in this topic, and it is how you check your own drawing: count the lines at each carbon and there must be four. A **displayed formula** shows **every** bond as a line, so methane is a C with four lines to four H atoms.

noteBlocks.prompt: In the displayed formula of methane above, how many bonds are drawn from the carbon atom?
noteBlocks.explain: Four. Carbon always forms four bonds, and checking that count is the quickest way to catch a wrong structure.

noteBlocks.title: Why the properties change gradually
noteBlocks.md: Each step along the family adds one more CH₂ to the chain. Bigger molecules attract each other more strongly, so it takes more energy to pull them apart and the boiling point rises. The chemistry stays the same because the bonds in the molecule are the same kind; only the size has changed.

noteBlocks.prompt: Members of a homologous series differ from the next one along by a ______ group.
noteBlocks.explain: CH₂. One more carbon and two more hydrogens each time, which is why the general formula works.

noteBlocks.md:
A **hydrocarbon** is a compound that consists of hydrogen and carbon **only**. That word *only* is worth a mark on its own, and it is the one examiners report being dropped year after year.
The **alkanes** are the hydrocarbon family with the general formula $\ce{C_nH_{2n+2}}$. They are **saturated**: every bond is a single bond. The first four are **methane**, **ethane**, **propane** and **butane**, and all four are **gases** at room temperature.

noteBlocks.prompt: Which of these is the full definition of a hydrocarbon?
options: a compound that consists of hydrogen and carbon only
a compound that contains hydrogen and carbon
a molecule made of hydrogen, carbon and oxygen
noteBlocks.answer: a compound that consists of hydrogen and carbon only
noteBlocks.explain: The word only is the second mark. Ethanol contains hydrogen and carbon too, and it is not a hydrocarbon, because it has oxygen as well.

noteBlocks.md:
**The question.** Draw the displayed formula of propane and give its molecular formula. **[3]**
**Step 1 — read the chain length from the name.** *Prop* means three carbons: meth 1, eth 2, prop 3, but 4.
**Step 2 — draw the carbon chain first.** Three C atoms in a row, joined by single bonds, because an alkane is saturated.

noteBlocks.prompt: Finish step 2. In the displayed formula of propane above, how many carbon-to-carbon bonds join the three carbons?
noteBlocks.explain: Two: one between the first and second carbon, one between the second and third. Three carbons in a chain always need two bonds to link them.

noteBlocks.md:
**Step 3 — fill every spare bond with a hydrogen.** The end carbons have used one bond each, so they take **three** H. The middle carbon has used two, so it takes **two**. That gives 3 + 2 + 3 = 8 hydrogens.
**Step 4 — write the molecular formula.** Three carbons and 8 hydrogens: $\ce{C3H8}$. Check it against the general formula: 2 × 3 + 2 = 8.

noteBlocks.prompt: Use the general formula C_nH_{2n+2} the same way for butane, which has four carbons. How many hydrogen atoms does it have?
noteBlocks.explain: 2 × 4 + 2 = 10, so butane is C₄H₁₀. Double the carbons, then add two.

noteBlocks.text: 5. Using the general formula on a big molecule

noteBlocks.md: The general formula earns its keep on molecules nobody draws. An alkane with 12 carbons has 2 × 12 + 2 = 26 hydrogens, so it is $\ce{C12H26}$. **Work the arithmetic out and write the finished formula** — examiners report answers left as "C₁₂H₂₄₊₂", which is a rule rather than a formula and earns nothing.

noteBlocks.title: GCSE Chemistry - Hydrocarbons - Alkanes & Homologous Series
noteBlocks.why: A second run through the family, the general formula and the names.

noteBlocks.prompt: An alkane has 7 carbon atoms. Use CnH2n+2 to work out how many hydrogen atoms it has.
noteBlocks.explain: 2 × 7 + 2 = 16. The rule works for any chain length, which is the whole point of having it.

noteBlocks.title: Where this mark goes
noteBlocks.md: Summer 2025's C2 Foundation report records the twelve-carbon alkane being left as an **unfinished formula** rather than worked out, and the name of the $\ce{C_nH_{2n}}$ family being given as *alkane* or *ethene* instead of **alkenes**.

noteBlocks.prompt: Which general formula belongs to the alkanes?
noteBlocks.explain: CnH2n+2 for the alkanes. CnH2n is the alkenes, and CnH2n+1OH the alcohols — worth keeping apart, because the paper asks you to name a family from its formula.

Stuck on a structure? Draw the carbon chain first and add hydrogens until every carbon shows four bonds. The Sheet below lists the traps.

steps.working: Eth means two carbons, joined by a single bond: C–C.
steps.decision: Chain first. The prefix gives the number of carbons, and an alkane is saturated so the link is a single bond.

steps.working: Each carbon has used one bond, so each takes three hydrogens: 3 + 3 = 6.
steps.decision: Count to four at every carbon. Six lines to H and one line to the other carbon means four bonds on each, which is the check that your drawing is right.

options: Because every carbon atom forms exactly four bonds
Because the formula has to end in an even number
whyMenu.explain: Carbon's four bonds fix the hydrogen count; you never have to remember it separately.

steps.working: Molecular formula: C₂H₆. Check with the general formula: 2 × 2 + 2 = 6.
steps.decision: Always check a formula against CnH2n+2. It costs five seconds and catches a miscount.

steps.working: From the Data Leaflet, Ar(C) = 12 and Ar(H) = 1.
steps.decision: Take both relative atomic masses from the leaflet rather than memory. A wrong Ar loses the Mr mark, though later steps still follow through.
Multiply each Ar by how many of that atom the formula has. Adding 12 and 1 once each is the commonest slip.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: (a) Two carbons joined by a single bond, with three hydrogens on each. (b) C₂H₆. (c) Mr = 2 × 12 + 6 × 1 = 30.

items.stem: How many covalent bonds does a carbon atom form?
items.skill: Prerequisite from C1 §1.4 — covalent bonding; you are not expected to have met the alkanes yet

options.text: four
options.feedback: Four. Every structure you draw in this topic is checked by counting to four at each carbon.

options.text: two
options.feedback: Oxygen forms two. Carbon has four outer electrons and forms four bonds, which is why its chemistry is so rich.

options.text: six
options.feedback: Six is the number of electrons in a carbon atom altogether, not the number of bonds. It forms four.

items.stem: In the formula C₃H₈, how many hydrogen atoms are there?
items.skill: Prerequisite from C1 §1.5 — reading a formula

options.feedback: The subscript after an element says how many of that atom the molecule has.
Three is the number of carbons. The 8 after the H is the hydrogen count.
That adds the two numbers. Each subscript belongs to the element in front of it.

items.stem: The Data Leaflet gives Ar(C) = 12 and Ar(H) = 1. What is the relative formula mass of CH₄?
items.skill: Prerequisite from C1 §1.9 — relative formula mass

options.feedback: 12 + 4 × 1 = 16. Every Ar is multiplied by the number of that atom in the formula.
That counts one hydrogen. The 4 in CH₄ means four of them, so add 4 × 1.
That multiplies the carbon by four as well. Only the hydrogens carry the subscript 4.

items.stem: Which of these is NOT a feature of a homologous series?

options.text: successive members differ by a CH₃ group
options.feedback: They differ by CH₂, not CH₃. One more carbon brings two more hydrogens with it.

options.text: they have the same general formula
options.feedback: That is one of the four features, so it is not the odd one out.

options.text: they show similar chemical properties
options.feedback: That is a real feature: the same bonds mean the same reactions.

options.text: their physical properties show a gradation
options.feedback: That is a real feature, and the boiling-point graph is the picture of it.

items.stem: What is the general formula of the alkanes?

options.text: CnH2n+2
options.feedback: Double the carbons and add two. It works for every alkane, however long.

options.text: CnH2n
options.feedback: That is the alkenes. The two extra hydrogens are what a double bond costs.

options.text: CnH2n+1OH
options.feedback: That is the alcohols, which carry an OH group. The alkanes have no functional group at all.

options.text: CnHn+2
options.feedback: The carbons are doubled first. For butane, 2 × 4 + 2 = 10 hydrogens, not 6.

items.stem: An alkane has 12 carbon atoms. What is its molecular formula?

options.feedback: 2 × 12 + 2 = 26. Work the arithmetic out and write the finished formula.
That is CnH2n, the alkene rule. An alkane needs the extra two hydrogens.
That adds 2 to the carbon count without doubling it first. Double, then add.
That is the rule half-applied. Summer 2025 examiners report exactly this: finish the arithmetic and write one number.

options.text: a compound consisting of hydrogen and carbon only
options.feedback: Both halves are marks: what it contains, and the word only.

options.text: a compound containing hydrogen and carbon
options.feedback: Without only, ethanol fits the description and it is not a hydrocarbon. That missing word is reported as a lost mark every year.

options.text: a molecule made only of carbon
options.feedback: Carbon on its own is graphite or diamond. A hydrocarbon needs hydrogen too.

options.text: a compound of hydrogen, carbon and oxygen only
options.feedback: Adding oxygen makes it something else — an alcohol or an acid. Hydrocarbons are just the two elements.

items.stem: How many hydrogen atoms are in the displayed formula of propane?

options.feedback: Three on each end carbon and two on the middle one: 3 + 2 + 3 = 8.
That gives every carbon two hydrogens. The end carbons have a spare bond each, so they take three.
That gives every carbon three. The middle carbon is joined to two other carbons, so it has only two bonds left.
Ten belongs to butane, which has four carbons. Propane has three.

items.stem: The first four alkanes boil at -162, -89, -42 and -1 °C. What is their state at room temperature, 20 °C?

options.text: all four are gases
options.feedback: Every one boils below 20 °C, so at room temperature all four have already boiled.

options.text: all four are liquids
options.feedback: A substance is liquid between its melting and boiling points. All four boil well below 20 °C, so they are past that already.

options.text: methane is a gas and the rest are liquids
options.feedback: Compare each boiling point with 20 °C: butane's -1 °C is still below it, so butane is a gas too.

options.text: it cannot be worked out from boiling points
options.feedback: It can, and this is how the exam asks it: above its boiling point a substance is a gas.

items.stem: Why do the alkanes have similar chemical properties?

options.text: they contain the same kinds of bond, so they react in the same ways
options.feedback: Same bonds, same reactions. Only the chain length changes along the family.

options.text: they have the same boiling point
options.feedback: Their boiling points differ, and that difference is the gradation in physical properties — a separate feature.

options.text: they all have the same number of carbons
options.feedback: The carbon count is what changes from one member to the next. The bonding is what stays the same.

options.text: they all have a functional group
options.feedback: Alkanes have no functional group, which is exactly why they are the least reactive family here.

items.stem: What does a displayed formula show that a molecular formula does not?

options.text: every bond in the molecule, drawn as a line
options.feedback: Every single bond on the page. That is why the marks are for the lines, not just the letters.

options.text: how many atoms of each element there are
options.feedback: The molecular formula already does that. The displayed formula adds the bonds.

options.text: the relative formula mass
options.feedback: Neither formula shows the Mr; you work that out from the Data Leaflet.

options.text: the state at room temperature
options.feedback: No formula shows the state. You get that from the boiling point.

parts.stem:
The first four alkanes are methane, ethane, propane and butane. The graph gives their boiling points.
Describe what makes the alkanes a homologous series, and explain how the graph supports your answer.
This question also assesses the quality of your written communication, including your use of specialist scientific terms.

bands.descriptor: Five or six of the indicative points, described in detail, with specialist chemical terms used widely and accurately; organised with clarity; spelling, punctuation and grammar good enough that the meaning is clear throughout.
Three or four of the indicative points; some specialist chemical vocabulary; organised with some clarity; spelling, punctuation and grammar competent enough for the meaning to be clear.
One or two of the indicative points; little specialist vocabulary; organisation may lack clarity; spelling, punctuation and grammar may leave the intended meaning unclear.

indicativeContent.point: They share the general formula CnH2n+2.
Successive members differ by a CH2 group.
They show similar chemical properties, because they contain the same kinds of bond.
Their physical properties show a gradation: they change steadily from one member to the next.
The graph shows the boiling point rising steadily as the chain gets longer.
The rise is steady rather than sudden, which is what a gradation means.
All four boil below room temperature, so all four are gases.

scheme.for: a banded answer covering the four features of a homologous series and reading the gradation off the graph: the shared general formula, the CH2 step, similar chemical properties, a gradation in physical properties, the steady rise in boiling point, and all four being gases at room temperature
scheme.examinerNote: A point contradicted elsewhere in the answer is not counted. Capital letters and full stops are part of the within-band judgement.

hints: Four features, then the evidence.
Use the graph for the physical half of the answer.
parts.workedSolution: The alkanes are a homologous series because every member has the same general formula, CnH2n+2, and successive members differ by a CH2 group. They show similar chemical properties, because each molecule contains the same kinds of bond and only the length of the chain changes. They also show a gradation in their physical properties, and the graph is the evidence for that: the boiling point rises steadily from methane to butane as each carbon is added, rather than jumping about. Every one of those boiling points is below room temperature, so all four alkanes are gases at room temperature.

findTheMistake.stem:
Aoife is asked: 'An alkane has 12 carbon atoms in its chain. Use the general formula of the alkanes to give its molecular formula, and name the family whose general formula is CnH2n. [2]'
Her answer:
studentWorking: The family with general formula CnH2n is the alkenes.
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: The two general formulae have been swapped in the first line. The alkanes are CnH2n+2, so a 12-carbon alkane has 2 × 12 + 2 = 26 hydrogens, not 24. The second line, which uses CnH2n for the alkenes, is right.
findTheMistake.feedback: One of the two marks. Naming the alkenes is right and stands. The alkane formula needs the +2: double the carbons, then add two, which gives C12H26. The two rules are one character apart, so write both at the top of the page before you start.

findTheMistake.stem:
Dara is asked: 'Explain the term hydrocarbon [2], and give the number of hydrogen atoms in propane [1].'
His answer:
studentWorking: A hydrocarbon is a compound that contains hydrogen and carbon.
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: The propane line is completely right. The definition is missing one word: only. As written it also describes ethanol, which contains hydrogen and carbon and an oxygen as well, and is not a hydrocarbon.
correction: A hydrocarbon is a compound that consists of hydrogen and carbon only.
findTheMistake.feedback: Two of the three marks: the second mark of the definition and the propane calculation both stand. The mark that goes is the word only, and examiners report it missing every year. Say the two elements, then say only.

prompts.answer: All four are gases, because every one of their boiling points is below room temperature, 20 °C.

prompts.prompt: Why do boiling points rise as you go along the alkane family?
prompts.answer: Each member has one more CH2, so the molecules are larger and attract each other more strongly, and more energy is needed to separate them.

findings.asked: Pick three features of a homologous series, name the family with general formula CnH2n, give the formula of a twelve-carbon alkane, and define a hydrocarbon.
findings.wentWrong: CnH2n was widely taken for the alkanes, or answered with a single compound's name. The twelve-carbon formula was sometimes left with its arithmetic unfinished. The definition of a hydrocarbon lost the word 'only', or called the carbon and hydrogen molecules rather than atoms.
findings.fullMarkAnswersDid: Kept the two general formulae apart, finished the arithmetic before writing the formula, and put the word 'only' into the definition.
findings.rule: Alkanes CnH2n+2, alkenes CnH2n; a hydrocarbon is hydrogen and carbon only.

findings.asked: The same definition of a hydrocarbon at Higher, with the identification of a homologous series from its general formula.
findings.wentWrong: The definition again lost 'only', and some answers described the carbon and hydrogen as ions.
findings.rule: A hydrocarbon is a compound of hydrogen and carbon atoms only.

findings.asked: Read four structures: which are gases, which is an alkane, name a four-carbon alkene, then draw butane.
findings.wentWrong: Few worked out that all four were gases; the structure of butane was drawn poorly; the names were confused with each other.
findings.rule: Count the carbons for the prefix and draw every bond as a line.

findings.asked: Organic chemistry across the whole section, including the physical state of propane.
findings.wentWrong: Giving the state of propane defeated many candidates, even with its boiling point in front of them.
findings.rule: Compare the boiling point with room temperature: below it means a gas.

insight.ruleToRemember: A homologous series shares a general formula, shows similar chemical properties and a gradation in physical properties, and steps by CH2. Alkanes are CnH2n+2, saturated, and the first four are gases; a hydrocarbon is hydrogen and carbon only. Draw the carbon chain first and add hydrogens until every carbon shows four bonds.
insight.aStarSignal: Moving freely between the name, the molecular formula and the displayed formula of any member, and using the general formula on a chain far beyond the four that are named.
